races.title: State Assembly, District 52
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Andrea Lee Anderson
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Assembly District 52 in 2026, challenging incumbent Jessica Caloza. She says her father was mayor of their hometown and her mother worked as a social worker and for the Girl Scouts. Her husband ran for Congress. No prior elected office or career is documented.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists Reform California, The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn, and several voter-guide groups (April's Common Sense Cali Voters, Based in Malibu, Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide) as endorsing or recommending her. Her own survey also names GBRA, PGRA and several individuals.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Anderson was born or raised, the name of her hometown, or when she moved to California. We found no record of her occupation or work history, and no earlier elected office. No news coverage or other independent reporting turned up, only her campaign site and her Ballotpedia profile. We found nothing documenting what she has done on any issue, only what she says. She has not stated positions we could find on data centers, farmland or growth limits, homebuyer limits for investors or foreign owners, gun laws, abortion, or teacher pay. Her stated tax position is about taxes generally, not property taxes. Her husband's run for Congress is mentioned without a name, year or district.

qual.background: Her own accounts describe a family of public servants and a husband who ran for Congress. Neither page gives her occupation or any elected or professional record.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Her campaign site says school choice is one answer to poor education, with parents controlling the state money for their child so they can pick a school, home school, or form a pod. It does not mention teacher pay.

workers-first.evidence: Her campaign site says immigration is the federal government's responsibility and the least California can do is cooperate with federal immigration agents rather than threaten them. It does not address H-1B visas.

back-police-order.evidence: Her campaign site says crime must be prosecuted. It calls for punishing theft and drug crimes more under Proposition 36 (repeal it or allow only one rehabilitation chance) and for enforcing existing laws against street camping and public urination and defecation.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: Her campaign site pledges to vote to lower taxes and promote a business-friendly environment. The pledge is about taxes in general; it does not mention property or homestead taxes.

cands.name: Jessica Caloza
cands.bio: Democratic member of the California State Assembly for District 52 since December 2024, and the first Filipina elected to the state Legislature. Previously Deputy Chief of Staff to the California Attorney General, Los Angeles Public Works Commissioner, an aide in Mayor Garcetti's Office of Immigrant Affairs, and a U.S. Department of Education policy advisor.

endorsements.text: California Democratic Party, California Nurses Association, California Teachers Association, California Professional Firefighters, Los Angeles County Federation of Labor, Planned Parenthood Action Fund, Sierra Club California and Brady: United Against Gun Violence (listed on her campaign site).

2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the California Federation of Labor Unions, California Environmental Voters, Equality California, Sierra Club Angeles Chapter, YIMBY Action, National Union of Healthcare Workers and California Young Democrats.

cands.gaps: We could not find where she was raised, when she came to California, or where she lives now, so her California ties are not scored. The pages do not list the bills she has authored, so we could not confirm specific legislative actions on data centers, property taxes, land purchases by investors or foreign buyers, immigration enforcement or H-1B, or policing. We found no stated positions from her on data centers or on property tax relief, and no documented controversies or foreign ties. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys. The pages give no statement on school vouchers or charter schools.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assemblymember since December 2024; Deputy Chief of Staff to the California Attorney General; Los Angeles Board of Public Works Commissioner from 2019; staffer in the Los Angeles mayor's Office of Immigrant Affairs; policy advisor at the U.S. Department of Education.
qual.why: She has held a legislative seat since 2024 and has a policy and government career at the federal, state and city levels, which fits the high band for a role that writes law and the budget. The pages show no chamber leadership beyond Assistant Majority Whip, so the score stays below the top of the range.

second-amendment.evidence: Says she is fighting for common-sense gun restrictions, including safe storage laws, and describes taking on the NRA and the gun lobby.

pro-life.evidence: Says she has fought to protect funding for Planned Parenthood and to expand access to health care for women, and lists protecting reproductive freedom as a priority.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Says she is fighting to raise wages for teachers and school support staff and to invest in public schools. The pages give no stated position on vouchers or charters.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Says she has fought for legislation to expand parks and open space and to protect clean air and water.
